items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: "How's Rosie? How's the baby?" Ten minutes they ask you about the family.

ctx.x: Were they people that had money?

They don’t have to have money. They’re just proud. Don’t want to associate. Poor as a church mouse. That’s poor. You can’t get no poorer than a church mouse, because there ain’t nothing to eat in a church. But they had this attitude. Wanted to look down on . . . fierce expression. You say, “Good evening.” They don’t even answer you, because they don’t want your good evening. You learn . . . I learned that first. I’ll tell you a good evening. You pass a bunch of people sitting on the stoops, and respect . . . well…

A lot of those values also went into the music. You talked about the Onward Brass Band. Tell me about that group, some of the better musicians in this city. At the time when you first saw them, were they reading or playing jazz, improvising?
